title: Image of ideal multiplication restricted to an ideal multiple of its tensor source
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], I a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], H a quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent], and n,m nonnegative integers. Let T=I^n \otimes H [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], mu:T \to H multiplication, and j:I^m T \to T the multiplication-image inclusion for the recursive ideal power [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. There is an isomorphism e:I^(n+m)H \cong image(j followed by mu) whose composite with the image inclusion into H is the higher-product inclusion. The higher power uses ideal-sheaf-data powers.

source.place: Tag 01YB, second Artin-Rees argument and last displayed map

proof.text: Prove quasi-coherence of the ideal realization by the affine basic-open localization criterion for its closed-subscheme pushforward, then quasi-coherence of its kernel. Tensor comparison and kernel/cokernel closure give quasi-coherence of all product and recursive-power objects. The affine pushforward argument is proved locally to avoid a circular import of proper-cohomology modules.

Tensor induction computes the affine product-inclusion range for any quasi-coherent ideal inclusion i. The generalized product lemma also maps this range through any module morphism phi, giving range(product inclusion followed by phi) = range(i) times range(phi). Quasi-coherence and an induction for arbitrary ideal inclusions compute all recursive-power ranges as range(i)^m, including zero via the identity inclusion. Transfer the abelian-image affine formula through an arbitrary isomorphic image presentation. Apply the product lemma with phi = mu directly to j followed by mu, and specialize the ideal range to I(U)^m. Multiplication has range I(U)^n H(U); hence the composite has range I(U)^m I(U)^n H(U) = I(U)^(n+m) H(U), which is the higher-product inclusion range.

On any topological basis of opens, sheaf separatedness detects zero morphisms. Consequently range containment for monomorphisms on that basis gives subobject containment: the composite with the other cokernel projection vanishes, and kernel lifting followed by the mono-image isomorphism gives a factorization. Specializing this general basis criterion to the affine basis and the equal computed ranges gives equal subobjects. Subobject.isoOfMkEqMk supplies the isomorphism; Subobject.ofMkLEMk_comp supplies its inclusion identity.

proof_origin.place: Tag 01YB, last displayed map; affine multiplication and local range comparison expanded in Lean by R2; repair generalizes duplicated helpers to composite ranges, arbitrary recursive ideal inclusions including zero, arbitrary image presentations, and arbitrary topological bases. The affine pushforward argument uses lower-level imports to avoid a source import cycle.

lean.statement:
theorem ideal_tensor_restricted_multiplication_image
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (I : X.IdealSheafData) (H : X.Modules)
    [H.IsQuasicoherent] (n m : ℕ) :
    letI : MonoidalCategory X.Modules := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory X.sheaf
    let T := (I ^ n).toModules ⊗ H
    let μ := (I ^ n).toModulesι ▷ H ≫ (λ_ H).hom
    let j := idealModuleProductι (idealSheafPower I.toModulesι m).2 T
    ∃ e : idealModuleProduct (I ^ (n + m)).toModulesι H ≅ image (j ≫ μ),
      e.hom ≫ image.ι (j ≫ μ) = idealModuleProductι (I ^ (n + m)).toModulesι H
